item.title: scFv developability metrics predict mRNA CAR-T function in primary T cells (Mangolini/Ramon/Sormanni, Cambridge/Imperial, Sci Rep 2026-07-19) — computational humanness/aggregation propensity/thermal stability/NSB metrics applied to FMC63, 14G2a, and MGA271 scFv families; aggregation-prone 14G2a markedly rescues CAR surface expression and cytotoxic activity under mRNA-LNP delivery; MGA271 optimization reduces off-target killing despite lower monovalent affinity; establishes developability engineering as rate-limiting step for mRNA-encoded CAR therapies. Lin/Huang (Zhejiang U, Oncogene 2026-07-16) — nanobodies against 4 distinct EGFR extracellular domain epitopes assembled into biparatopic and triparatopic formats; triparatopic forces EGFR clustering, dynamin-dependent endocytosis, and lysosomal degradation; triparatopic > biparatopic > osimertinib in TKI-sensitive and osimertinib-resistant NSCLC xenografts; mechanism extends to PD-L1 crosslinking. Duprez/Sanofi NANOBODY Platform (mAbs 2026-07-16) — nanobody A0445046C08 (KD <23 pM for human MerTK) blocks ADAM17-mediated ectodomain shedding without competing with Gas6 binding or inhibiting MerTK kinase; half-life-extended version A044500050 reduces soluble Mer levels in Zymosan sterile peritonitis mouse model; proof-of-concept for substrate-selective shedding inhibition with single-domain antibodies
item.description: Sunday edition — three journal papers, all about engineering specificity through geometry. First, Mangolini/Ramon/Li/Souster/Hayre/Karattil/Sormanni/Onuoha (Cambridge Centre for Misfolding Diseases + Imperial College London + Chimeris UK; Scientific Reports DOI 10.1038/s41598-026-60295-2, published 2026-07-19): developability engineering of scFvs for transient mRNA-LNP CAR-T delivery. Motivation: unlike stable viral transduction, mRNA delivery provides a single expression burst; aggregation-prone or biophysically deficient scFvs that can compensate over time under stable expression have no such buffer — the fraction that misfolds, aggregates, or fails trafficking before reaching the membrane is a permanent loss. Three scFv families chosen to span the biophysical quality spectrum: FMC63 (anti-CD19, stable/monomeric, backbone of axi-cel/liso-cel), 14G2a (anti-GD2, aggregation-prone murine-derived sequence), MGA271/chBRCA84D (anti-B7-H3, intermediate baseline quality). Computational workflow: humanness scoring by germline database comparison, aggregation propensity via CamSol solubility predictor, thermal stability from sequence-based predictors, non-specific interaction propensity (NSB). In silico humanization variants generated, scored across the multi-axis developability profile, top variants forwarded to cell-based testing in primary human T cells via mRNA-LNP delivery. Results: FMC63 — optimization improved humanness and thermal stability but functional readout (CAR surface expression, cytotoxic activity) essentially unchanged; already biophysically adequate, incremental gains within a permissive quality space produced no functional shift. 14G2a — parent aggregation-prone scFv showed poor CAR surface expression and impaired cytotoxicity against GD2+ targets after mRNA delivery; computationally optimized variant with markedly reduced CamSol aggregation propensity rescued both CAR surface expression and cytotoxic function; aggregation propensity was the rate-limiting failure mode. MGA271 — optimized variants had lower NSB scores and reduced off-target killing; monovalent affinity to B7-H3 reduced (standard cost of removing hydrophobic surface character), but on-target B7-H3+ killing preserved while off-target signal dropped; developability and selectivity engineering aligned. Full text behind journal paywall from this machine; summary grounded in abstract + Sormanni-group published methodology (CamSol, Cambridge Antibody Developability Assessment). Second, Lin/Liu/Ni/Chen/Liu/Zhu/Sheng/Wang/Gao/Zhang/Ma/Liang/Huang (Zhejiang University Life Sciences Institute + Xiamen U Pharmaceutical Sciences + Zhengzhou U Thoracic Surgery + Biochee Biotech Xiamen; Oncogene DOI 10.1038/s41388-026-03901-x, published 2026-07-16): multiparatopic nanobody antibodies bypass TKI resistance by inducing lysosomal EGFR degradation. Design rationale: monomeric antibodies binding one epitope on a cell-surface receptor predominantly return the receptor to the surface through normal recycling; receptor clustering — crosslinking multiple receptor copies simultaneously — promotes dynamin-dependent endocytosis and shifts endosomal fate toward lysosomal degradation rather than recycling. Implementation: nanobodies generated against 4 distinct EGFR extracellular domain epitopes; assembled into biparatopic (2 nanobody units, 2 epitopes) and triparatopic (3 units, 3 epitopes) antibody formats. Mechanism: epitope-dependent EGFR clustering → endocytosis → lysosomal degradation; degradation process is epitope-combination-dependent and dynamin-dependent. In vitro: potent suppression of downstream signaling (ERK, AKT phosphorylation) and cell proliferation in NSCLC lines carrying diverse EGFR mutations including osimertinib-resistant C797S; triparatopic format consistently outperforms biparatopic on receptor clearance. In vivo xenografts: triparatopic > biparatopic > osimertinib in TKI-sensitive and TKI-resistant lines; triparatopic + osimertinib additive (antibody removes receptor, inhibitor suppresses residual kinase in fraction that escapes degradation). Generalizability: antibody-mediated crosslinking triggers lysosomal PD-L1 degradation by the same mechanism, establishing receptor elimination by multiparatopic clustering as a general strategy for pathogenic cell-surface proteins. Engineering implication: epitope combination for cluster geometry is a distinct design variable from single-epitope affinity optimization; triparatopic nanobody fusion chains are compact enough to remain manufacturable as single polypeptides. Full text behind journal paywall; summary grounded in abstract. Third, Duprez/Kilic/Bruwiere/Fekir/Vlaeminck/De Craene/Geiregat/Paesen/Leutenez/Lambrecht/Van De Velde/Moliere/Verhelst/Stuyven/Hoelper/Schmoll (Sanofi Large Molecule Research NANOBODY Platform Ghent + Sanofi R&D Frankfurt; mAbs DOI 10.1080/19420862.2026.2704449 / PMC13378718, published 2026-07-16): substrate-selective blockade of MerTK ectodomain shedding by a single-domain antibody. MerTK (Mer tyrosine kinase, TAM family) mediates efferocytosis — phagocytic clearance of apoptotic cells — which is anti-inflammatory. ADAM17-mediated ectodomain shedding removes the extracellular MerTK domain from the cell surface; shed ectodomain (sMer) circulates as a decoy receptor sequestering Gas6/Protein S ligands away from membrane-bound MerTK; cell-surface stub after shedding is non-functional. Therapeutic hypothesis: nanobody that sterically blocks ADAM17 access to the MerTK cleavage site from the substrate side, preserving ligand binding and kinase activity. Nanobody A0445046C08: KD <23 pM (human MerTK by SPR, below instrument floor), <40 pM (cynomolgus MerTK). In primary macrophages (LPS stimulation): IC50 1.2-1.6 nM for MerTK shedding blockade. Selectivity confirmed: does not compete with Gas6 binding; does not activate Erk1/2; does not inhibit ADAM17 enzymatic activity at active site (steric near cleavage site, not protease inhibition). Half-life extension: A044500050 — one or two MerTK-binding nanobody units + C-terminal albumin-binding nanobody ALB23002; IC50 3.7-5.5 nM in macrophages; humanized MerTK/Gas6 transgenic mice in Zymosan sterile peritonitis model: dose-dependent reduction of sMer in peritoneal lavage fluid at 3 mg/kg and 10 mg/kg. Pharmacological design concept: substrate-selective shedding inhibition from the extracellular side avoids pan-ADAM17 inhibitor on-target toxicity (ADAM17 sheds TNF, HER2, amphiregulin, and many other substrates); single-domain antibody format is geometrically suited for narrow juxtamembrane cleavage-site access that conventional antibody CDR loops cannot reach. First clean in vivo proof-of-concept for this strategy with a nanobody. Full text accessed via PMC.
item.itunes:summary: Mangolini/Ramon/Sormanni/Onuoha et al. (Cambridge/Imperial/Chimeris UK, Sci Rep 2026-07-19): developability engineering of scFvs for mRNA-LNP CAR-T delivery. Three families spanning biophysical quality spectrum: FMC63 (stable/monomeric → minimal functional gain), 14G2a (aggregation-prone → markedly improved CAR surface expression and cytotoxicity after CamSol-guided aggregation propensity reduction), MGA271 (reduced NSB and off-target killing despite lower monovalent affinity). Key finding: under transient mRNA expression, biophysical quality of scFv is rate-limiting — aggregation propensity fixes translate directly to function in primary T cells. Establishes computational developability metrics as necessary pre-cell-work filter for mRNA-encoded CAR programs. Abstract-only (paywall). Lin/Huang et al. (Zhejiang University, Oncogene 2026-07-16): multiparatopic nanobodies against 4 EGFR extracellular domain epitopes assembled into biparatopic and triparatopic formats. Clustering-induced EGFR endocytosis and lysosomal degradation — epitope-dependent, dynamin-dependent. Triparatopic > biparatopic > osimertinib in TKI-sensitive and osimertinib-resistant NSCLC xenografts; additive with osimertinib. Mechanism extends to PD-L1 crosslinking — receptor degradation by multiparatopic clustering is a general design strategy for pathogenic cell-surface proteins. Epitope combination for clustering geometry is distinct from single-epitope affinity optimization. Abstract-only (paywall). Duprez/Sanofi NANOBODY Platform (mAbs 2026-07-16): nanobody A0445046C08 (KD <23 pM human MerTK) blocks ADAM17-mediated MerTK ectodomain shedding at IC50 1.2-1.6 nM in primary macrophages without competing with Gas6 binding, activating Erk1/2, or inhibiting ADAM17 active site. Half-life-extended A044500050 (albumin-binding domain ALB23002 fusion) reduces sMer in Zymosan peritonitis mouse model dose-dependently (3 and 10 mg/kg). First in vivo proof-of-concept for substrate-selective shedding inhibition with a single-domain antibody — concept extends to any membrane protein with pathogenic ectodomain shedding (shed TNFR, BCMA, ErbB4).
